facts: A line of best fit passes as close as possible to as many points as possible.
It has roughly equal numbers of points above and below it.
Draw it so the distances of the points from the line are as small as possible overall.

A line of best fit is only appropriate when the scatter plot shows a roughly linear trend.
steps: Look for the overall linear trend in the scatter plot.
Draw a single straight line through the cloud of points, following the trend.
Balance the line so roughly equal numbers of points sit above and below it, staying as close to all the points as possible.
Stop the line at the edges of the plotted data — do not extend it beyond the data range.

mastery.solution_text: No — the two end points lie on the line, but all the interior points lie above it. Although it follows the downward direction, the line is too low and does not have a roughly balanced split of points above and below it.

The line is straight, stays within the data range, and has $5$ points above it and $3$ below — so far it looks acceptable.
But several points sit far from the line: at age $1$ the point is about $\$3\,000$ above the line, and at age $8$ it is about $\$3\,000$ below it, because the line is much flatter than the data's actual downward trend.
A good line of best fit must also keep the distances of points from the line as small as possible — this line fails that test even though it passes the other three.
